title: Shunyu Wu (吴舜禹)
text:
I am a Ph.D. candidate in the Department of Automation at Shanghai Jiao Tong University. I study learning methods that connect prediction with downstream decisions, especially time-series forecasting and resource scheduling in urban water and water-energy systems.

I examine which forecast errors alter the selected action or schedule. Depending on the application, I evaluate the model by operating cost and optimality gap, demand-trend timing, or pressure error.

title: Shunyu Wu (吴舜禹)
text:
Research


Decision-focused learning for water-energy scheduling
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize passes probabilistic electricity-cost forecasts to a stochastic scheduler for urban water supply. A convex upper bound on the resulting optimality gap, derived from Lagrangian duality, provides gradients for predictor training.


Forecasting under lag and unobserved disturbances
The knowledge-based bi-correction model uses lag-penalty attention and a masked weighted Markov chain to correct delayed responses in daily water-demand forecasts. CritiCoder separates the modeled response to observed variables from residual pressure variation represented as an uncertain disturbance.


Learning-based action and trajectory selection
Current collaborations study candidate-action selection in offline reinforcement learning and diffusion-based trajectory generation conditioned on local LiDAR geometry. GEM reranks sampled actions at inference, whereas DRIFT retrieves waypoint-specific scene context during recurrent denoising.


More detail is available on the Research page.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Daily demand near turning points
Daily urban water-demand forecasts can attain low average error while responding late when demand changes direction. This lag reduces their value for planning the next operating period.
The knowledge-based bi-correction model addresses the problem in two stages. Lag-penalty attention extracts prior sequence and feature information associated with timely demand changes. A stacked LSTM produces the primary forecast. A masked weighted Markov chain then corrects selected residuals using posterior error information.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Trend-sensitive evaluation
The study introduces mean prediction trend effectiveness to test whether a model follows changes in demand more closely than a naive forecast. Reporting this metric alongside absolute-error measures separates response timing from average numerical accuracy.

title: Urban water forecasting and pressure modeling
text:
Pressure under unobserved variation
CritiCoder considers macroscopic pressure when measured inputs do not explain every disturbance in a water distribution system. The Coder models the pressure response associated with observed variables. The Critic changes the loss so that the remaining pressure variation can be represented as an uncertain disturbance.
The comparison tests whether CritiCoder’s error increases less than conventional regression error at nodes more strongly affected by unobserved disturbances.

title: Research
text:
Decision-focused training for water-energy scheduling
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize addresses electricity-cost uncertainty in water-energy resource scheduling. The model combines probabilistic forecasting with a stochastic scheduling problem for urban water supply. Its training objective uses a differentiable convex upper bound on the optimality gap derived from Lagrangian duality, so forecast distributions are evaluated by the schedules they induce.
This line of work examines which forecast errors alter the optimal schedule and how a constrained solver can provide a training signal. It also tests whether lower operating cost or regret comes at the expense of forecast calibration.

title: Research
text:
Time-series forecasting at turning points
The knowledge-based bi-correction model targets lag in daily urban water-demand forecasts. Lag-penalty attention extracts sequence and feature information associated with timely changes. A stacked LSTM produces the initial forecast, and a masked weighted Markov chain corrects selected residuals using posterior error information.
The same study introduces mean prediction trend effectiveness to test whether a model follows the direction of demand changes more effectively than a naive forecast. This metric complements absolute-error measures because a low average error can conceal a delayed response near a turning point.

title: Research
text:
Pressure modeling with unobserved disturbances
CritiCoder models macroscopic pressure when measured inputs do not explain all disturbance-related variation. Its Coder estimates the response to observed variables, while the Critic modifies the training loss to represent residual variation as an uncertain disturbance. The study evaluates this separation across monitoring nodes with different exposure to unobserved disturbances.

title: Research
section: Explicit selection rules for learned decisions
text:
Explicit selection rules for learned decisions
Two 2026 collaborations extend this interest beyond water systems. GEM uses a Gaussian-mixture actor to retain multiple action hypotheses in offline reinforcement learning. At inference, it ranks a candidate set with an ensemble lower-confidence bound and a behavior-support term standardized within the current state.
DRIFT generates trajectories from local LiDAR observations. Structured Scene Perception stores local geometry as graph memory. During recurrent denoising, the model retrieves waypoint-specific geometry and conditions each update on the target.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text: This page summarizes the peer-reviewed article and omits utility names, asset locations, internal screenshots, and operational records.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Decision problem
Urban water supply consumes electricity throughout treatment, transport, and distribution. The resulting schedule depends on the expected electricity cost, while errors in that forecast can change operating cost and the selected schedule.
The study models the full water-supply process as a stochastic scheduling problem with uncertain electricity prices. It evaluates forecast quality by pointwise prediction error and by the objective value of the induced schedule.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize
Stochastic Predict-Then-Optimize combines a probabilistic forecasting model with the downstream stochastic program. The forecast distribution supplies uncertain cost parameters to the scheduler. The resulting schedule defines the decision loss used to update the predictor.
Direct differentiation through this optimization problem is difficult. SPTO+ replaces the exact optimality gap with a differentiable convex upper bound derived from Lagrangian duality. The bound supplies a surrogate gradient while retaining the scheduling problem in the training objective.

title: Water-energy resource scheduling
text:
Evaluation
The experiments compare forecast quality, operating cost, and decision regret on real-world water-supply systems. The paper reports lower operating cost and regret than the tested two-stage forecasting and optimization baselines. The public article does not disclose the utility maps or operational dashboards previously stored in this repository.
